subject: CHEMISTRY
pageTitle: Dilution Equation (M₁V₁ = M₂V₂): How to Dilute a Solution
description: Use M₁V₁ = M₂V₂ to find how much stock solution to use, then add water to the final volume, with two worked chemistry examples.
caption: Dilution in 7 swipes: M1V1 = M2V2, what each letter means, and two worked examples. Save this for your solutions unit. Free Chemistry study guide at precisstudy.com/chemistry (no sign-up).

slides.title: HOW MUCH STOCK SOLUTION DO YOU NEED?
HOW TO USE IT
lines: Know three of the four values
Use the same volume units on both sides
slides.note: Moles of solute stay the same when you add water.

slides.title: EXAMPLE 1
slides.problem: How many mL of 6.0 M HCl make 250 mL of 1.5 M HCl?

slides.title: EXAMPLE 2
slides.problem: You dilute 50 mL of 2.0 M NaCl to 200 mL. What is the new molarity?

slides.title: WATCH OUT
slides.wrong: Add 250 mL of water to the stock
points: V₂ is the final total volume, not the water you add.
Add acid to water, not water to acid.
